messages:
sam: FYI — we've got a customer reporting streaming responses that cut off mid-chunk, then the connection closes. Happens when their client is slow to read.

jordan: Can you paste the logs? Are we seeing EAGAIN/EPIPE on the socket?

sam: Yep, from the edge worker logs: 
```
[2024-04-11T22:03:12.431Z] ERROR stream_write: writev returned -1 errno=EAGAIN, sent=0 conn_id=cn-7f3 model=redwood-lite
[2024-04-11T22:03:12.432Z] WARN stream_abort: aborting stream conn_id=cn-7f3 reason=slow_consumer buffer_used=4.1MB
```

kevin: That WARN matches our backpressure threshold kicking in. If the client isn't draining the socket the runtime aborts to avoid OOM/latency spikes for other requests.

emily: Customer says this is intermittent — large responses sometimes, small ones fine. They use a mobile client behind flaky cellular.

sam: Repro steps I used: start a streaming request, then run a slow reader: 
```bash
# simulate slow consumer (reads 128 bytes every 250ms)
python tools/slow_reader.py --url "https://api.redwood.test/v1/stream" --sleep 0.25 --auth "$TOKEN"
```
Client sees a few chunks then socket closes. Edge logs show repeated EAGAIN then an abort after ~30s.

jordan: Two potential culprits: (1) our send buffer limits + aggressive abort policy, (2) proxy (customer side or our edge) buffering + backpressure mismatch. Which edge region?

sam: us-west-2, edge host host-11. Traces attached to the ticket (trace id tr-9a8).

eng-runtime: quick notes from runtime: default write loop will attempt sendv up to N bytes and if >M consecutive EAGAINs we mark connection as slow_consumer and trigger stream_abort to keep token latency SLOs. We do this intentionally to protect headroom.

kevin: For support path: ask the customer to try enabling TCP keepalive and reduce per-chunk size (client-side) as mitigation. Also provide a temporary server-side knob: increase slow_consumer abort window for their org (requires config change and a risk note).

emily: Customer also flagged billing — they were charged for partial responses. They want retries or idempotent resume.

jordan: We should document the behavior: when a stream is aborted due to backpressure we currently emit a 499/connection-aborted and billing is per-token generated. We can offer to refund specific cases but long-term we should have explicit resume tokens for streaming.

sam: I posted a repro script in the ticket. Also saw proxy logs showing NGINX upstream timed out while buffer full: 
```
nginx: 2024/04/11 22:03:12 [error] 12345#0: *789 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 1.2.3.4, server: , request: "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:9000/stream", host: "api.redwood.test"
```

eng-runtime: That points to proxy-level buffering. For streaming we expect chunked transfer and minimal buffering; NGINX default proxy_buffering can make the upstream think it's writable while client is clogged. We recommend disabling proxy_buffering for streaming routes: 
```nginx
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
}
```

kevin: Action items: 
- Support: offer interim refund and mitigation steps to customer (disable buffering, client reduce chunk size, enable keepalives)
- Eng-runtime: evaluate increasing abort threshold for this org and add a per-tenant flag
- SRE: check edge host-11 send/recv sndbuf settings and tcp_autocork.

emily: I'm sending the refund approval now and added a note to the billing team with trace id.

jordan: Small follow-up: can we add extra debug telemetry when we emit slow_consumer? e.g., current sendq bytes, consecutive_eagain_count, buffer_high_watermark. That will make triage faster.

eng-runtime: Agree. I'll add a one-line metric and a log field in the next patch. For now I can whitelist their org id to relax the abort path for 48h.

sam: Thanks — I'll patch the ticket with the mitigation steps and the whitelist. Customer on the line for a call in 30m; will ask them to try nginx tweak and the slow_reader script while we monitor. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: NOTE: host-11 tcp_sndbuf=212992 tcp_rcvbuf=212992. Consider increasing net.core.wmem_max for high-latency mobile clients.

kevin: Great. If call goes poorly ping me and I'll pull in runtime to do a live config flip.

emily: Customer confirmed that disabling proxy_buffering resolved the immediate disconnects in the trial. We'll keep the whitelist and follow up with a product ticket for resumable streams. :white_check_mark:
